performance.matureComparisonWindow: 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-16; all Oct17 posts excluded from creative judgments
unavailable: Facebook attributed follows, saves, views and watch time
performance.conclusion: Reels distribute materially better than carousel or single images, but seven mature days generated zero Instagram follows. No evidence yet of follower growth. Stop repeating static ominous ruins and opaque unanswered-object mysteries after three or more weak comparable posts. Test tangible human agency, visually resolved action, warmth and practical fantasy-scale consequences; maintain ongoing serial continuity without judging Oct17 before 24h. The Oct16 Highward Reel earned 2 saves but no follows, so saves alone do not validate growth.
performance.historicalClue: Change + conflict + mystery + concrete stakes; do not copy historical sea-isolation caption.

prompts.reel1: Use case: illustration-story. Asset: ORIGINAL The Land of Roo discovery Reel scene 1, vertical 9:16. Cinematic Nordic fantasy realism, tactile handwoven wool and tarred timber, emotionally legible at phone size. In a small clinker-built sailing boat pulled into a rocky fjord cove, a tall pale HUMAN woman aged 35 with long wavy black hair tied low, gray eyes, muted teal wool tunic and a large deep crimson wool cloak, holds up her beautiful cloak beside a badly ripped cream square sail lowered across the boat. The tear in the sail and the cloak are the two connected story elements, she has a decisive expression, cold wind, slate-blue water and wooded cliffs. A tall pale HUMAN male companion with long blond hair, short beard and brown wool jacket braces the spar in the middle background. Medium close composition woman waist-up and cloth centered, faces and tear between 25 and 75 percent of canvas height, sky upper 18% and deck lower 15% clear for later text. Low sun brightens crimson fabric against cold fjord, no gloomy mud. No text, no logos, no modern objects, no armor, no horned helmets, no Arven or nonhuman people, no magic or glowing symbols, no slavery or collars. Newly imagined small local scene, no named canonical characters, no borrowed footage.
prompts.carousel1: Use case: illustration-story. Asset: ORIGINAL The Land of Roo carousel frame 1, portrait 4:5, no text. Cinematic highly detailed Nordic fantasy concept art, tactile natural materials, forest greens and warm russet. In Roo's exceptionally lush autumn forest, a tall pale HUMAN forager woman aged 45 with long copper-red braid, oatmeal linen shirt, moss-green wool sleeveless overdress and russet shawl, stands alongside ONE enormous brown porcini-shaped mushroom with a cap as wide as her outstretched arms and its base already harvested and resting in soft moss. She holds one ordinary small wicker basket in front of it, visibly comically inadequate, looks from basket to huge mushroom with a wry delighted smile. All single focal idea: basket far too small for bounty. Mushroom not anthropomorphic, no eyes or creatures. Rich towering spruces, fern banks, ordinary mushrooms secondary. A faithful local visual exploration of Roo's oversized fertile plant life, not a new named species or official scientific scale. slots.title: The Cloak That Carried Them Home

captions.instagram:
She cut up her best cloak.

The sail had torn. Home was still across the fjord.

Stitch by stitch, her crimson wool became their way back. By sundown, that red patch was the first thing their neighbors saw.

Would you have cut yours?

The Land of Roo is an original Nordic fantasy world being created by Thomas Robbjens. Follow the continuing story.

captions.facebook:
Her best cloak became the way home.

A torn sail drove two Rooan travelers into a sheltered cove. They had thread, a needle—and the crimson wool she had worn for years.

She cut the cloth. Together they stitched it over the tear. By sundown, a red patch was carrying them toward the timber houses across the fjord.

Would you have sacrificed your best cloak, or waited in the cove?

slots.title: The Wrong Basket
alts: A red-haired human forager holds an ordinary wicker basket beside an enormous brown mushroom in Roo's lush forest. Text: She brought the wrong basket. Swipe to see how it got home.
The same forager and a friend haul the harvested mushroom in a wooden handcart, with the small basket hanging from its side. Text: One mushroom. Two friends.

captions.instagram:
She brought the wrong basket.

Roo's forests grow on a generous scale—even the mushrooms. In this imagined harvest, one find was more than she could carry.

Swipe: she came back with a cart and a friend. Supper was no longer just for one.

What would you make: soup or pie?

captions.facebook:
One basket was never going to be enough.

Trees, moss and mushrooms grow unusually large in Roo's fertile forests. This imagined harvest turns that detail into a very practical problem: how do you get such a find home?

The second image has her answer—a handcart, a friend and enough to share.

If you were cooking supper in this fantasy hall, would you choose mushroom soup or a pie?

slots.title: Fireside Tales of Roo — She Chose Her Own Guide
alts: A young honey-blond human traveler in a blue embroidered dress, fur mantle and new red scarf walks beside the silver-haired innkeeper in rust and brown clothing on a snowy forest road. Fresh bootprints mark the path.

captions.instagram:
She chose company, not another command.

Fireside Tales of Roo

A stranger had drawn a doorway from her dreams. She burned his drawing rather than follow him. Now the innkeeper offered to show her the road.

“How do you know it?”
“I grew up in the house beside it.”

The traveler accepted a warm scarf. “Then walk with me.”

For the first time, the journey felt like her own.

At the first bend, another set of bootprints marked the snow. Who else had taken that road this morning?

Follow for tomorrow's fireside tale.

captions.facebook:
This time, she chose who walked beside her.

Fireside Tales of Roo

At a snowbound inn, a stranger drew the doorway a young traveler kept seeing in her dreams. She burned his drawing rather than let him choose her path. When she finally told the innkeeper, the older woman recognized the place.

“How do you know it?” the traveler asked before leaving.
“I grew up in the house beside it.”

The innkeeper offered her a warm scarf. The traveler accepted it.
“Then walk with me.”

They left side by side. Her fear had not vanished, but the decision was hers.

At the first bend, they found another set of bootprints. Who else had taken that road this morning?

Follow for the next part tomorrow.
